newsitem.title: UK: Merrill, DMG in running to lead Matav offer - sources.
newsitem.headline: Merrill, DMG in running to lead Matav offer - sources.

text.p: Investment banks Merrill Lynch and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are in the running to lead the international offering for Matav, the Hungarian national telecommunications company, banking sources said on Thursday.
"Two banks -- Merrill and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell -- are being proposed to the Matav board but no decisions have been made yet," one bank industry source said.
The Financial Times said in Thursday's edition that Merrill was set to lead the Matav offering.
It added that Deutsche MG and Credit Suisse First Boston may play a leading role in the European tranche but the source said the CSFB reference was inaccurate.
"Two banks, rather than three, have been proposed," the source said.
However, a spokeswoman for CSFB insisted it was still being considered for the flotation.
In December, Hungary's transport and telecommunications minister Karoly Lotz said Matav was likely to be listed on the Budapest stock exchange and a major foreign bourse in November.
Around 17 percent of Matav is expected to be floated. Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech together own 67 percent of Matav.
A spokeswoman for Merrill Lynch said the company had no comment on the report. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was unavailable for immediate comment.
